ratings_why.fun: Hold-or-clear debt is a real choice every turn, and the pawnshop replay is a joy, but the Ledger asks a lot of rules before the first card pays off.
ratings_why.distinct: Earns 8 over 7: debt is a visible resource that pays you for holding it (Eldest, interest-fed Collect), for clearing it (Joy, Corbie), and when other players pay it (Skim, feathers, protection). No tribe today or in Battlegrounds plays like that.

verdict_why: Cards read cleanly and the crime-family fantasy lives in what they do; the one fix is a single golden line, and more rounds would only reshuffle.

points.text: Golden Seven's "Counts as paid twice" doesn't say what doubles. Say it plainly, e.g. "each gold of interest Seven pays fires Collect twice".
The Ledger has about eight rules (cap, sixth-IOU merge, interest, shortfall, fresh ink, full amount). Let the slip UI carry the edge rules so card text only needs IOU, Borrow, Collect and clear.
Scolding Jackdaw is three clauses in one paragraph. Break it into short lines: who gets a feather, who your units hit first, what a feathered death pays.
Mr Magpie's bad-luck line sits inside the rules text. Move it to italic flavour so the card reads "When played: write an IOU 2."
Uncle Jack's triple clause leaves an IOU with nothing behind it; a few words saying clearing it returns nothing would stop players hunting for the missing unit.

standouts.why: Gallows Lane Enforcer is the protection racket as a mechanic: other tribes' units pay your debt and get Shield for it. Reads in one glance.
Uncle Jack makes the pawnshop real: cash a unit now, get it back and replay it when you pay up.
Corbie's Eldest is the simplest card in the tribe and says the whole hold-the-debt idea: more slips, bigger family.

weakest.why: Silver-Spoon Magpie's six-keyword steal list is long to read and loosely tied to the Ledger.
Wassail Warden's bowl moves one slot per Collect; with many Collects a player can't tell at a glance who ends up with what.
The Magpie in the Mirror is a plain copy card; the mirror-test flavour doesn't show in what it does.

flags.note: Golden text "Counts as paid twice" has no clear meaning for Collect.
Memory with Seven, Warden and Clerk on a full Ledger stacks many Collects a turn; worth the owner's eye.
Sorrow can offer a Tier 6 copy for 1 gold at Tier 3 after one loss.
